transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 986 Creekhaven Drive?
Yeah, this is me at 986 Creekhaven Drive—just me and two others, no one’s stuck inside, and I’ve got a boat handy if we need to get out, no truck though.
Thanks for confirming your address and safety status. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
There are three people here total, and everyone’s able to be at the phone—no one’s stuck inside or can’t leave alone.

Thanks for letting us know everyone is able to be at the phone. Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own, not even a wheelchair or oxygen user—everyone’s good to go, and we’re all able to move around fine, no motorized chairs or anything like that.
Thanks for confirming everyone can move around safely. Is there water inside the home right now?
No water inside at all, just a dry house, and I’m good to go—no one’s stuck or needing help leaving, and I’ve got a boat ready if needed, though no truck.
Thanks for the update—stay safe and ready. If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
Yeah, I’ve got a boat ready to go if anyone needs a ride out—just let me know, I’m at 986 Creekhaven Drive, and I’ve got three people here, no one’s stuck alone, and the water’s not in yet.
Thanks for offering help and sharing your situation. Let me read that back: 3 people; no water inside yet; you can help with a boat and 3 free seats. Is that right?
Yeah, that’s right—three people here, no water in yet, and I’ve got a boat ready to go, though no seats are taken right now.

Thanks for confirming your situation and readiness. I've recorded that you may be able to help neighbors. A dispatcher may contact you. Only go out if it's safe for you, and never drive into water you can't see the bottom of. Goodbye.
